pick.angle: Lead with the finding that 81 of 101 directories offered a free option, then use the submission log to show why free does not mean frictionless—or guarantee a live dofollow backlink.
pick.why_share: Makers will share a concrete launch-planning reference that exposes badge requirements, review queues, inbox steps, and ambiguous confirmations while clearly separating submission outcomes from verified listings and the nonrandom link-attribute sample.

outline:
- **Title:** "81 of 101 directories offered a free option. Here is what happened"
- **Opening answer block:** Lead with 81 of 101 directories offering a free option, then distinguish free submission from a published listing or live dofollow backlink. Keep this block within the first 50 words.
- **Measurement and author disclosure:** Identify Jason T. as the maker of AgentoolRank, a directory of open-source AI agent tools ranked by live GitHub activity. Attribute the findings to our submission notes for three products, collected by hand and browser automation from 2026-09-29 through 2026-10-02, last verified 2026-10-02. Define the sample as 101 sites where at least one product entered the submission flow, with one submission per site per product and no captcha-solving services.
- **## What happened across 101 directories**
  - Use a small outcome table: 66 submitted or already listed; 19 skipped for rules or fit; 9 queued for retry after the first attempt failed; 5 stopped at a visible captcha; 2 stopped over a required free-tier badge.
  - Make clear that "submitted or already listed" does not mean 66 newly published backlinks.
- **## Free options still come with conditions**
  - Report conditions across the 101 sites: 56 review queues, 14 badge requirements, 12 backlink requirements, and 1 required X post. Do not treat these as mutually exclusive categories.
  - Ground waiting-time expectations in Viesearch's 1,200+ queue and stated 82% free-tier rejection rate, SaaSHub's wait of up to 32 days, and TinyLaunch's scheduled free launch on 2026-11-02.
  - Note that 39 sites showed a price, with a $12 median entry price. Use Findly.tools' possible delisting after badge removal to explain ongoing obligations.
- **## A free listing does not guarantee a dofollow link**
  - Lead with the sampling limitation: rel attributes were recorded on only 30 sites, usually when something looked off. Results were 23 nofollow, 6 dofollow, and 1 ugc, not an estimate for all 101.
  - Use the recorded examples: AlternativeTo and LaunchBoosts free-plan links are nofollow; make.rs profile links use `rel="ugc nofollow"`; AI Agents Directory's free links are nofollow, with dofollow starting at $49.
  - Recommend inspecting a live listing before counting a dofollow backlink, without claiming SEO outcomes.
- **## Budget for human steps and uncertain confirmations**
  - Report 30 sites needing inbox access, 19 offering or requiring Google login, and 8 presenting a captcha requiring a person. Distinguish those 8 from the 5 captcha-blocked outcomes.
  - Describe the concrete traps: dismiss FutureTools' popup with "No thanks"; claim SaaSHub management access before closing the browser; check spam for Viesearch, then click "Join the Waiting List" and "Wait in Line."
  - Explain why automation needs follow-up: only 75 sites gave clear confirmation, including FutureTools' "Tool Submitted!"
- **## How to plan your own submission run**
  - Recommend checking conditions before filling forms, reserving time for inbox and captcha steps, and maintaining a dated per-site log of results and blockers.
  - Set expectations: very little referral traffic observed so far; no promise of traffic, publication, or ranking gains.
  - Close with our [free comparison of where to list an AI agent tool](https://agentoolrank.com/where-to-list), the invitation "If a site's rules changed, tell us and we update the data," and the signature "Jason T."
  - End with a short disclosure: "Disclosure: The linked comparison is ours."
inferred_rules_initial: That made free submission common in our log, but it did not guarantee a published listing or a live dofollow backlink.
They do not turn every completed form into a published backlink.
"Submitted or already listed" needs to stay intact as a label.
It does not mean 66 newly published backlinks.
That still takes attention, even though it produces no listing.
Likewise, the 9 retries are unfinished work, not confirmed failures or successes.
A submission run needs somewhere to record those states without quietly counting them as done.
If your launch checklist says "submit to 100 directories," decide what completion means before you start.
These are not mutually exclusive categories.
Do not add them together as though each site had only one condition.
Those are Viesearch's displayed figures, not a rejection rate measured across our products.
Neither belongs in the same mental bucket as a listing you can inspect immediately after submitting.
That figure describes the displayed entry prices; it says nothing about whether paying would be worthwhile for your product.
If there is a queue, record the expected wait instead of treating the submission date as the publication date.
A free listing does not guarantee a dofollow link
This was not a random sample, so the results should not be used to estimate link types across all 101 directories.
A confirmation message does not answer that question, and neither does the existence of a free tier.
This is also why I would keep submission status separate from link status in a log.
You can know that a form went through without yet knowing what the published link will look like.
Our observations do not establish SEO results or ranking gains.
The login and captcha counts should not be added to that as if there were no overlap.
No clear signal is not proof of failure.
Automation can handle parts of the run, but our log gives no basis for treating the whole process as unattended work.
Neither publication nor ranking gains should be assumed.
inferred_rules_final: If you accept that condition, it becomes something to remember when changing your site, rather than a box to tick once.
That is a concrete case where "free listing available" and "free dofollow link available" are different claims.
Start by deciding which conditions you are willing to accept.
Treat a review queue as pending work, with a follow-up date where the directory gives you a useful waiting period.
Have a way to pause for a person instead of losing track of the site.
Keep "submitted," "already listed" and "needs checking" distinct, so you can follow up without submitting twice.
The next useful step is choosing which conditions fit your launch, before opening more forms.
